suggestions.reason: This assertion passes as long as the status field is 'complete', but doesn't verify that all six steps have timestamps or that accumulated-context was populated. A workflow that wrote status=complete without running the steps would pass. Consider adding a check that step_timings contains all 6 entries.

suggestions.assertion: Structural assertions were run and results written (assertions_checked > 0 for at least one record)
suggestions.reason: The threshold is 'at least one record' which is trivially satisfied. The run asserted 3 records. A stronger assertion would check that assertions were run on all records that have a definition file available — or that no record with a known assertion definition was skipped.

suggestions.assertion: The workflow opened and closed its own self-tracking eval record
suggestions.reason: Passed, but the actual outcome was two records (PCHVJ1 unclosed + GVFJWB as a 'closed' new record). A clean open/close cycle was not achieved. The assertion should check that exactly one self-tracking record transitions from in-progress to closed, not just that a closed record exists.

No assertion checks whether the grades assigned are substantive (not just a letter, but with grader_notes content). A workflow could write grade='B' with empty notes and pass all expectations. Expectation 2 could be strengthened: 'At least one grade was assigned with non-empty grader_notes.'

No assertion covers the score_eval.py race condition — a real data quality issue that the run self-reported. An assertion checking that the scored grades match the assigned grades (post-grading) would catch this class of bug.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-targeted for a smoke test but rely heavily on qualitative transcript reading. The two file_exists checks (analysis report, dashboard) are the only objectively verifiable assertions. The qualitative assertions could be strengthened with file content checks (e.g., grader_notes non-empty, state.yaml has 6 step_timings entries, self-tracking record count). The date-alignment gap in daily-review assertions — flagged honestly in the run itself — is not caught by any expectation here, representing a known harness weakness with no coverage.
